v.text: Log reset at Steven's request. The prior 25 entries (2026-09-04 through 2026-09-07 — the Sep 4 reset, the property-tax and search features, the AI Team build-out, the specialist expansion, the mentors, the design-system pass, the live-data sync, the FERS Dual-Pension Engine and federal salary calculator, the TradingView integration section, the accessibility slider, and the sync-engine reload-loop fix) were exported to command-deck-ci-log-backup-2026-09-07.json in ~/Applications before clearing, so the history is recoverable. From here this log tracks continuous-improvement changes going forward.

Local news: the five footprint cities that had been seeded empty (Murrieta, Menifee, Riverside, Orange County, New Braunfels) were showing a permanent 'Connecting live headlines…' placeholder — the live You.com fill has no failure path, so when the search capability isn't granted or errors, nothing ever replaces the placeholder. Two fixes: (1) each of the five now ships with real, dated, sourced headlines pulled today (Murrieta e-bike parent-liability ordinance and the AB 2307 signal-sync pilot; Menifee kratom lawsuit and Labor Day DUI patrol; Riverside's Fairmount Park encampment crackdown, RTA hydrogen buses and the $32M body-camera buy; OC coastal erosion ahead of El Niño and the Ladera Ranch pesticide push; New Braunfels' Klein Road completion and the Brauntex marquee debate), so the cards are never blank; (2) the live wiring now falls back honestly — if live search is unavailable or errors, the note reads 'Snapshot synced <date> — live refresh isn't available in this view' (or the error code, retrying on the next interval) instead of hanging. Daily News refresh routine continues to rotate the seeds.

AI Hedge Fund Team, incorporated and made to work remotely. Steven installed the /ai-hedge-fund-team skill with seven dedicated Claude Code agents (market-scout, technical-analyst, fundamental-analyst, news-analyst, quant-analyst, risk-manager, portfolio-manager). Ran it for real on AAPL: gathered primary raw material first (Apple's Jul 30 press release, the SEC 10-Q for the quarter ended Jun 27, 2026, a 2-year daily price file from Yahoo Finance, seven dated headlines through Sep 7, the Sep 9 event / Sep 15–16 FOMC calendar), then the seven roles in strict order, each handing its report to the next. The coordinator's verification pass (Step 8 of the skill) caught a material error before anything was shown: the aggregator's trailing EPS ($7.47) was a quarter stale — the four company-reported quarters sum to $8.72 — so the committee's '42.8× true trailing P/E' thread was an input error; the vendor's 36.7× was right. The 10-Q also corrected the share count (14.594B, not 14.715B), the nine-month buyback ($62.2B) and resolved the vendor debt/equity conflict (0.78). The Portfolio Manager re-issued the memo on the corrected inputs (research rating: Neutral, leaning cautious; Medium confidence). Dashboard changes in Markets & Trading: (1) a Committee Memo card that renders the latest run — memo, all six reports, the verification log, and sources — from the synced db document hfCommitteeMemo (seeded with the AAPL run; a newer remote run always wins); (2) a Remote Run card: type a ticker → saved to the synced doc hfRequest → a new cloud routine ('AI Hedge Fund Team remote run', Mondays 5:00 AM PT, or Run now from claude.ai/code/routines on any device) reads the pending request, runs all seven roles with Bash-computed quant stats and primary-source verification (including the rebuild-TTM-EPS-from-four-quarters rule learned today), writes the memo back to the dashboard, updates the request status, and pushes one notification; plus copy buttons for /ai-hedge-fund-team in Claude Code. The memo is registered in the freshness board (7-day threshold). Research only — the committee never trades and nothing it writes is advice.

Vanessa repositioned to the top of the page, at Steven's request. The Chat with Vanessa card (chat thread, starters, reach table) and the Vanessa's recommendations card moved out of panel 19 (AI Employees & Digital Twin) into a new pinned section directly under the greeting, above the Morning Brief. The section carries no page tag, so it stays visible on every tab and is untouched by tab switching; the shared thread, specialist routing, and recommendation flow are unchanged (same element ids, same synced keys). Panel 19 keeps a pointer card that jumps to the new position.

ISA line — live two-way communication with the human EA/ISA, plus alerts. Steven asked for a way to talk with his real ISA from the AI Team portal, for the ISA to reach him, Vanessa, the AI team and his digital twin from the ISA Portal, and to be alerted on the dashboard to anything immediate. Built: one shared, append-only thread ('isaLine') that exists in both dashboards' databases with identical message ids; each page appends to its own copy and merges (never replaces) what arrives from the store, so nothing can be dropped by either side. A new cloud routine, 'Command Deck ↔ ISA Portal comms bridge' (hourly; Run now from claude.ai/code/routines on any device), unions the two copies with a deterministic script, stamps relayedAt on what crossed, merges read receipts, writes both back only where they differ, and pushes a phone notification for anything new from the ISA — urgent items and decision flags are called out. Command Deck (AI Team, first card): the thread, Send as Steven / Vanessa / Steve with a priority, and Draft · Vanessa / Draft · Steve buttons that put a draft in the box for Steven to edit and approve (human-in-the-loop; nothing sends itself). ISA Portal (AI Team, first card): the ISA picks a recipient — Steven (relayed), Vanessa, Steve (the twin) or the AI team via Vanessa — and a priority (Normal / Urgent / Needs Steven's decision / FYI); Vanessa and Steve answer live on the portal with ISA-scoped context and the whole exchange is copied to Steven; Steve ends every answer with a NEEDS STEVEN flag, and a 'yes' automatically raises a decision item for Steven. Alerts on Command Deck: urgent messages and decision flags appear in the bell, the executive exception report, and a pinned 'ISA line: N unread' pill at the top of every tab; an ISA ask left unanswered 4h+ and a bridge that hasn't carried a message in 3h+ also raise exceptions; the browser tab title shows the unread count; Vanessa's live snapshot now includes the line. Copy buttons give a near-live /loop 10m bridge for Claude Code and a one-off bridge prompt for any Claude session. Verified end to end: the first message (Steven → ISA) was carried into the ISA Portal's store and stamped as delivered. Found and recorded honestly: a cloud routine can READ an artifact database unattended but its WRITE asks for an approval tap, so the hourly routine only completes after that one-time approval (its first run is parked waiting for it); the local /loop path has no such prompt and is the dependable one today.

Income streams: the single 'Social Security / Post-9/11 Ed benefit (future)' row was split into two rows — 'Social Security (future)' keeps the existing amount and key, and a new 'Post-9/11 GI Bill education benefit (future, tax-free)' row starts at $0 for Steven to fill in. FERS Dual-Pension Engine: the VA disability compensation table now shows its as-of line (VA.gov rates effective Dec 1, 2025 — the 2026 table — verified by hand today against va.gov: 10% $180.42 … 100% $3,938.58 alone; the with-spouse column matches too), carries a VA_COMP_SYNCED_AT stamp on the freshness board with a 400-day threshold, and is refreshed every January by the existing 'FERS engine + federal salary calculator annual refresh' routine, which already re-fetches VA.gov each run.

Apple Health connected end to end (Health & Wellness). Steven asked for the Apple Health section to track every Health Auto Export category — Activity, Body Measurements, Hearing, Heart, Mindfulness, Mobility, Nutrition, Reproduction, Respiratory, Sleep, Vitals, Other — fed from the iPhone through the Mac. Pipeline that already existed: Health Auto Export → REST POST → apple-health-mcp ingest daemon (LaunchAgent, port 8765, bearer token) → DuckDB → the apple-health MCP server. Found while wiring it: the daemon is healthy but the database was empty — the phone's automation pointed at the Mac's old LAN address (192.168.1.83; it is .84 today), so no export had ever landed. The setup card now gives the Bonjour address (STEVENs-MacBook-Pro.local:8765/ingest) so the router can't break it again. New on the page: twelve category tiles that render whatever metrics arrive (latest value, date, 7-day average, week-over-week change; nightly sleep with stages and efficiency; 7-day workouts), a Refresh from this Mac button that asks the local apple-health MCP for one summary query when the dashboard is open in the Claude desktop app, copy buttons for refreshing from any Claude session (a snapshot script was added to the repo, scripts/health_snapshot.py, running the identical SQL), a Fill Health-metrics log button that populates weight, resting HR, sleep and steps for the last 14 days without overwriting typed values, freshness-board tracking with a 2-day threshold, and alerts in the bell and exception report when the export pipeline stalls. Nothing is fabricated: until the first export lands, every tile says so. One limit found at publish time: declaring the local host:apple-health MCP grant is refused on the page's pinned runtime contract (0.2.31), so the Refresh-from-this-Mac button stays pending until Steven chooses to move the page to the latest contract; the Claude-session refresh path works today.

Apple Health: batch Excel/CSV import. Steven asked for a batch of Excel files to populate every field on the Apple Health card. The card now has an Import button that accepts any number of Health Auto Export Excel or CSV files at once (SheetJS is loaded from the allowed CDN only when an Excel file is chosen; CSV is parsed in-page). Every column is mapped by its header — the metric name, the unit in parentheses, and any [Min]/[Max]/[Avg]/[Systolic]/[Diastolic] qualifier — into the same snapshot shape the live pipeline produces: latest value and date, 7-day and prior-week statistics, per-day totals for the log filler, sleep nights rebuilt from In Bed/Asleep/Core/Deep/REM/Awake columns, and workouts from a workouts sheet. Imports merge into the existing snapshot (newer values per metric win; nights and workouts de-duplicate) and sync to the other devices. A per-file report shows what each sheet contributed and which columns were skipped, so nothing is silently dropped. This path fills the dashboard only; the Mac database is still fed by the live REST export.

Prop firm operations: automation-policy note. Steven supplied a research summary of which futures prop firms allow algorithmic or bot-driven trading and which restrict it on funded accounts (Topstep/TopstepX conflicting reports, MyFundedFutures July-2025 policy, Tradeify Select accounts, Alpha Futures / Take Profit Trader / FundedNext / TradeDay, Lucid / Phidias / Blusky / Bulenox, and Apex's funded-account ban on set-and-forget automation). It now sits as a callout directly under the named prop firm table, with the firms Steven actually holds accounts at tagged, the semi-auto vs fully-auto distinction spelled out against the QZeus and Archangel X bots, the three source links, and a visible reminder that these are third-party summaries dated Sep 2026 to be confirmed against each firm's own rules.

Freshness sweep + weather/news cadence. Steven asked for news and weather to refresh at least three times a day and on every browser refresh, and for every feed marked Due to be updated now. Weather and news: the page previously claimed two cloud routines kept them fresh; those routines do not exist (the registry comment already said so), and cloud routines cannot do it anyway — this evening's Steve-twin run sat 100 minutes on an artifact-data permission prompt before its write went through, so an unattended cloud writer is not dependable. The fix is a desktop-app scheduled task, Weather + news refresh (3x/day), at 6 AM / 12 PM / 6 PM PT that writes weatherSnapshot and newsSnapshot docs to the synced store; the page now prefers those docs over the seed baked into the file, and the live You.com pull runs with no cache replay so every page open and browser refresh re-fetches (then re-polls every 15/30 minutes while open). The task only runs while the Claude desktop app is open; a missed slot runs at next launch. Feeds refreshed by hand this pass with sources: Bears (Week 1 injury report), QuantVue strategies and stacks re-read from the live sheet (sizes/YTD/MTD moved, Trofe strategy and Equal Weighted Tiers 2 and 5 added 9/2), loan program facts (2026 funding-fee tiers, San Diego $1,104,000 and Riverside $832,750 county limits, MIP), top performers (Sep 4 session), Follow Up Boss (live pull: stage counts, 39 contacts created in 90 days), builder incentives (NewHomeSource Temecula answered — 7 builders / 29 communities named; Murrieta/Menifee pages blocked and said so), Elite rewards (bonuses re-confirmed, MGM and military status matches added), PE & Defense (TITAN, Hanwha/Austal, Lockheed/Ultra Maritime, Ondas/DYZNE, PitchBook H1 stats), Opportunity Radar (ROAD to Housing Act disclosures, TITAN), Next Big Moves weekly review (facts refreshed, recommendations unchanged, SPACE site still down with HTTP 525) and Marketing (Monday routines ran). Four sync notes that claimed daily automatic refreshes now say Claude session research pass, which is the truth.

Institution directory: login + password columns, Plaid live balances, freshness times. Steven asked for login and password columns on the Institution & alternative-asset directory and a Plaid connection for live balances. Login is a normal synced field. Password is a device-only vault: it lives under a separate browser-storage key outside the dashboard's sync prefix, so the sync engine, the JSON backup and every connector and routine never see it — it will not appear on other devices, which is the point; the real record belongs in a password manager. Plaid: Link cannot run inside this page (security policy blocks Plaid's script and all network calls) and Composio has no Plaid toolkit, so a local bridge was built at ~/Applications/plaid-bridge (FastAPI, plaid-python, offline tests): institutions are linked once on its localhost link page through Plaid's own window, access tokens stay in a 0600 file on the Mac, and a snapshot script emits the plaidBalances document that any Claude session writes to the store. The directory now shows each row's live balance, account count and as-of time, a manual mapping dropdown when Plaid names an institution differently, a relink badge on ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED, and rows that are not Plaid institutions are marked manual. Plaid errors and stale snapshots raise alerts. Still needed from Steven: Plaid API keys in the bridge's .env and the first link. Also removed the Magica MCP status badge from the AI tooling table, and the Data freshness table now shows the time next to each synced date (Pacific) where the feed records one.

Vanessa as orchestrator + the reporting layer. Steven asked for Vanessa to orchestrate the C-suite, for the executives and AI employees to work in parallel, and for reports under the C-suite where needed. Built as a skill (/vanessa-orchestrator), 21 agent definitions on the Mac (vanessa-orchestrator, the seven executives, and thirteen reports: lead-triage-analyst and deal-desk-analyst under Victor; bookkeeper and tax-deadline-analyst under Marcus; content-writer and webinar-producer under Sofia; automation-engineer and data-steward under Derek; ad-compliance-reviewer and trid-timeline-checker under Alexandra; research-analyst under Nadia; phishing-triage and access-auditor under Elena), a Friday desktop scheduled task that runs the Weekly Ops Review and writes vanessaRuns / vanessaRecommendations / twinQueue, and a Friday cloud routine as the off-Mac fallback that researches and pushes but only writes when approved. Every agent ends with the same contract (facts, assumptions, recommendation, deliverable, needs-Steven) and carries the standing guardrails: draft/analyze/recommend only, licensed activity stays Steven's, no invented numbers, no credentials. The roster on this panel now shows the reporting lines, and the in-page Vanessa consults every relevant specialist in the same turn and points to the orchestrator for full runs.

Part 9 of the automation audit is now on the deck: the twelve things that were missing. Three new panels. Ops Radar (Daily) carries speed-to-lead — median first response against the 5-minute standard, with a hand-log so it works before the watchdog exists — plus the automation health table and backup status, each with a copyable refresh prompt and an honest empty state naming what would fill it. Practice Trackers (Real Estate) carries licenses and filings seeded with the real NMLS/DRE/CE/E&O/Statement of Information/BOI items and the Q3 TX-VA-NC window (dates deliberately blank, to be filled from the source document) with alerts at 60, 30 and 7 days; a refi rate-watch that computes each past client's spread against today's rate for their program off the Daily rates card and flags 75 basis points; referral partners by metro against the two-to-three-per-metro, signed-agreement, quarterly-call standard; per-file transaction checklists that build the six-phase coordinator timeline from the contract date; a review pipeline; the LPT recruiting pipeline with the rev-share tiers; and the webinar funnel with show rate, consult rate and cost per consult against the 105-120 registration and 50-seated targets. Money Housekeeping (Wealth) carries the subscriptions audit with monthly and annual totals, and the beneficiary review seeded with the real accounts, flagging anything over a year unverified. Everything raises alerts into the bell and the exception report; nothing invents a number.

News, weather, market and calendar feeds refreshed by a Claude session at Steven's request ("fix everything that is stale, no staleness anywhere"). Weather: all seven cities pulled live from api.weather.gov. liveFeeds: all 17 lists rewritten from web research with dated facts and citations. newsSnapshot: 5 global headlines and 4 items for each of the 11 cities. marketSnapshot: replaced the Sep 4 card with the Fri Sep 18 close - Dow 51,682.64 (-95.40), S&P 500 7,650.50 (+12.74), Nasdaq 26,522.55 (+104.25), from the AP wire as carried by three outlets, cross-checked against an independently reported Thursday close. calendarSnapshot: read live from Steven's connected Google Calendar (Personal, SPACE, and the USC Canvas-import calendar). Not touched: the separate Sep 7 AI-news seed card, and everything personal or Mac-synced.

Reset-token bug found and fixed (engineering check requested by Steven). Four docs - ciLog, marketSnapshot, aiNews, and (already-safe) hfCommitteeMemo - carry a 'reset once per token' migration guard from when this page first shipped. Three of the four (ciLog, marketSnapshot, aiNews) unconditionally overwrote the doc with its hardcoded launch-day default the moment ANY browser loaded the page with a mismatched token in that browser's local storage, regardless of what real synced content already existed. That is what erased this log's own Sep 20 entry and the Sep 18 market close within minutes of each being written, and it did so a SECOND time (this entry included) while the fix was rolling out: an already-open browser tab was still running the pre-fix script and fired the old destructive overwrite one more time using the newly-bumped token, right after the fix was published but before that tab reloaded. The fix removes the overwrite entirely from all three - only the token bookkeeping remains, since lsGetSeeded already falls back to each doc's default on its own when nothing is stored, so the forced overwrite never served a real purpose once live synced data existed. hfCommitteeMemo's own reset was already safe (it only seeds when nothing newer exists) and needed no change. Both affected docs have been restored a second and final time on top of the fixed code (published), which can no longer perform this overwrite under any token value.

Loop Cycle 6 — a full audit-and-remediate pass run by twelve engineers working in parallel git worktrees, each owning one region of the deck and each gated by the same two tests. 205 findings, 61 P1. THE TWO THAT MATTERED MOST WERE BOTH ABOUT MONEY AND BOTH SILENT. The VA 30-year rate on this page read 6.125% while the daily feed it claims to read said 6.751% — 62 basis points wrong on a licensed originator's dashboard, because the rates card had a hand-baked seed the render never replaced. And the year-over-year price change had NEVER once refreshed: the feed writes yoy as the string "+5.7%", the parser expected a number and returned null, so San Diego showed +2.4% under a current-looking timestamp. Both now re-bake from ratesSnapshot with per-row sources, and a USDA row the seed never had. CRM: Steven retired Follow Up Boss for Lofty. FUB had in any case been rejecting its API key on every call since Sep 16, and the freshness stamp read leadTriage.ranAt — which is written even when the run FAILS — so six days of authentication failures had been rendering as a fresh import. Zoho was tested live and returns 403 NO_PERMISSION Crm_Implied_Api_Access; the card now carries that exact error and the one-line fix instead of a hardcoded red badge. RELIABILITY, from a stress sweep of 61 tests: the ISA line merge silently discarded any message without an id — on a two-way channel with a person, that is lost correspondence; a document written without the {v:...} wrapper was skipped on restore, so a full recovery returned 160 of 161 documents and the missing one was the Strava sync; every local save failure was swallowed by an empty catch, so a full browser store looked exactly like a successful save. All four fixed and re-tested against the test that found them. ROUTINES: thirteen of fifty cloud routines had a failed or hung last run, every one of them dying 5 to 10 seconds after firing and every one of them inside two crowded windows — Friday 20:00-23:00 and Sunday 15:00-17:00 UTC. Contention against the weekly quota, not broken logic. Five were destaggered, three duplicate weekly loops were consolidated into one, and six created in the web interface are listed for Steven because an agent cannot edit those. NEW: panel 39, Orchestration and Loop Engineering, on its own tab — the master findings table, the stress test report, the CPI and scale logs, the trust gate with the halt conditions in full, the weekly brief, and a roadmap derived from the open findings so the two can never disagree. Every table names the task that was supposed to fill it when it is empty. Also: the second brain rebuilt as files a Claude Code session actually loads (a router that sends an agent to exactly one leaf per question), twelve skills written, and the org chart updated with the model tiering — Fable masterminds, Opus judges, Sonnet executes, Perplexity researches.
